name: Hate Waste
definition: Leaders find ways to do more with less. We save costs rather than simply cut them. We do not skimp on a penny today if that will cost us a dollar tomorrow.

rows.situation: When the budget has to come down
rows.under: Cuts the line item and lets the work it funded fail somewhere else.
rows.justRight: Finds the way to get the same outcome for less, so the cost goes rather than the outcome.
rows.over: Redesigns everything to save an amount that will never show up in the accounts.

rows.situation: When the cheap option has a tail
rows.under: Takes the cheap option and pays for it every month afterwards.
rows.justRight: Counts what the choice costs over its life, not what it costs to buy.
rows.over: Justifies any spend today with a long-term saving nobody will ever check.

rows.situation: When the meeting has 20 people in it
rows.under: Invites everyone, in case they are needed.
rows.justRight: Treats other people's hours as a real cost, and invites who decides and who does.
rows.over: Cuts people out of decisions they have to carry out, and pays for it in rework.

rows.situation: When the spend would make the team faster
rows.under: Refuses, because the line item is visible and the lost hours are not.
rows.justRight: Spends where it buys speed or safety, and is tight everywhere else.
rows.over: Buys every tool anyone asks for and calls it investing in the team.

rows.situation: When work is being done that nobody uses
rows.under: Keeps producing the report because it has always been produced.
rows.justRight: Finds out who reads it. If nobody does, stops it.
rows.over: Kills a cheap artifact that a small group depended on, without asking them.

rows.under: Lets cost grow with volume and calls it the cost of growth.
rows.justRight: Drives the cost per unit down as volume rises, so growth funds itself.
rows.over: Starves the capacity that growth needs, and turns a good quarter into an outage.
